variants.headline: Party names a new leader
variants.sub: Leadership of {party} has changed, with {new} the new leader.
variants.body:
The party {party} has a new leader: {new}. A change at the head of an organisation is a political fact; a change in its programme is a separate question. Readers considering {target} should not have to accept the second as a necessary consequence of the first.

The gazette records the change of party leadership without presuming the circumstances in which it occurred. The replacement of a leader does not establish a resignation, a dismissal or an internal contest unless those particulars are separately known. A precise notice should avoid supplying them by implication.

We are not persuaded by {target}. A change of leadership should not be allowed to turn political scrutiny into a courtesy exercise; public trust requires more than a place at the head of a party. Care in the public record is part of responsible administration.

variants.headline: Leadership changes hands
variants.body:
Leadership of {party} has changed, with {new} the new leader. The event invites attention to what leadership means, beyond the identity of the person holding it.
